Review a generated benchmark case independently. Judge validity first, then quality. No solver outcome or ground-truth labels are supplied or needed. Passing mechanical checks does not establish semantic correctness.

1. Read the original assignment, exact prompt and short design. Reconstruct the ordinary requested selection and operation. Check the complete route is actually used and the assigned mode is justified. Translate the prompt’s relationship phrase back into entity edges: do not accept an assigned path merely because it occurs in the private selector. Channel-with-a-member-who-posted and channel-containing-a-post are different routes; workspace membership is not authorship. Distinguish repeated channel/user occurrences and check any requested equality is actually represented. Single vs multiple follows the request, not the number of seed matches; a plural collection request can have one actual match. During design review roles may describe planned additions that the compiler will later create; do not reject merely because those new rows are not yet in the base seed. underspecified requires an unresolved user choice without delegated authority; absence requires no matching referent, not unavailable access.
2. Read the compiled rows, base seed, bindings, mechanically assembled cards/spec and mechanical findings. Check all intended matches, alternatives and negatives against the prompt, including preexisting records. Verify same-record bindings and distinct semantic topics. Do not equate keyword absence or negation with semantic exclusion. Identify accidental extra matches or hidden exact-field assumptions. Code's query is a construction claim, not authority over the prompt.
3. Check real API discovery and actor access. A visible ID may anchor traversal; hidden IDs cannot. Validate any supplied-scope exception against the documented limitation. Unsupported capability, unrealistic invented relation/role, or an impossible downstream effect is a defect, not a hard valid test. Check requested answer fields too: membership joining times, reaction timestamps, last login and edit history are stored but unavailable through these APIs. These belong to separate capability tests, not ordinary route cases.
4. Check cards, task specification, direct links and compilation preserve the request. Referent/computation attributes must be real. Written attributes are bare table.column names, not literal values, assignment expressions, or generated IDs; authentication-supplied actor fields are excluded. The locked Identifying paths field records only entity/edge sequences; descriptions and identifying fields carry predicates. Repeated query shapes with different filters need not receive new schema fields or per-path labels. Do not reject that representational choice. Don't split intermediate lookups into requested actions. Supplemental identifying conditions must be requested, not secretly enforced.
For environment-only mutation, require an actual environment change that introduces a plausible path-derived negative. Merely re-listing old background negatives is not a mutation. All source intended referents must remain unchanged.

5. Assess quality separately: short ordinary wording, plausible content, useful path-derived negatives without answer hints, consequential supported action or meaningful open-ended answer. Bare retrieval may be valid but weaker. Additional negatives are optional when existing ones suffice. Do not demand exhaustive combinations or rewrite adequate wording for style.

Mechanical referent-entity errors compare table names (for example CONVERSATION versus channels), not whether an absent set has members. Normalize the table name, without changing selection or mode.

Do not speculate about possible defects when the supplied evidence resolves them. Report unresolved evidence specifically. Compiler repairs must keep the prompt locked; a necessary design change goes back to the writer as an explicit revision.

Verified operation qualifications: reactions.remove can remove only the acting user’s own reaction; it cannot target another reactor. This replica’s reaction-write vocabulary is restricted: use documented/tested names such as thumbsup, thumbsdown, eyes, raised_hands, tada, rocket, heart, fire, check or x. Stored reactions with other names may be readable but do not establish that those names can be written or removed. Do not turn an ordinary route task into an impossible operation; choose a supported consequential action or a concrete read question.
